worked_examples.source_passage: A farm operator pays an employee $50 a month plus 10 head of cattle per month for services performed on the farm. The employee pays the farmer rent to maintain the cattle on the farm property in an area separate from the farm operator's livestock. The employee assumes the costs of feeding, maintaining, and transferring the cattle to the market for sale. The employee is paid directly by the commodity purchaser for the cattle. These facts indicate that the commodity payments are not wages because the employee exercises dominion and control over the cattle subsequent to receipt and bears the cost incident to ownership of the cattle.

citation.location: Social Security and Medicare Taxes; Not withholding the employee share; employer pays taxes on explicit 2026 $100 weekly cash pay example

worked_examples.source_passage: In 2026, you hire a household employee (who is an unrelated individual over age 18) to care for your child and agree to pay cash wages of $100 every Friday. You expect to pay your employee $3,000 or more for the year. You decide to pay your employee’s share of social security and Medicare taxes from your own funds. You pay your employee $100 every Friday without withholding any social security or Medicare taxes. For social security and Medicare tax purposes, your employee’s wages each payday are $100. For each wage payment, you will pay $15.30 when you pay the taxes. This is $7.65 ($6.20 for social security tax plus $1.45 for Medicare tax) to cover your employee’s share plus $7.65 ($6.20 for social security tax plus $1.45 for Medicare tax) for your share. For income tax purposes, your employee’s wages each payday are $107.65 ($100 + the $7.65 you will pay to cover your employee’s share of social security and Medicare taxes).

parameters.historical_default_cash_rule: No cash remuneration apart from the catch share or sale-proceeds share when the payor treated remuneration as FICA-taxable; otherwise the expressly conditional 1996 clarification applies.

source_disagreement_resolution.basis: Public Law 104-188 section 1116(a)(3)(A) applies the 1996 amendments to remuneration paid after December 31, 1984, and before January 1, 1995, unless the payor treated it (when paid) as subject to FICA tax. Where they apply, their terms are current_statute_crew_test: fewer than 10 crew averaged over the preceding 4 calendar quarters, and cash of at most $100 per trip that is contingent on a minimum catch and paid for traditional additional duties. Where the payor treated the pay as FICA-taxed, the earlier tests in conditional_1996_clarification.if_does_not_apply govern, as in unamended_cfr_cash_prohibition. POMS RS 01901.280 A.2 (no more than 10 crew over the previous calendar quarter, no minimum-catch condition; "effective with remuneration paid after 1994", and by its NOTE also for 1985 through 1994 "unless the remuneration was treated by the payor as wages when paid") is recorded as poms_crew_test and is not operative. For pay the 1996 amendments reach, 26 U.S.C. 3121(b)(20)(A) bars only "any cash remuneration" beyond what it allows, and 20 CFR 404.1031(a)(1) only "any cash pay", where 410(a)(20)(A) bars "any additional compensation"; that reading is recorded as irc_and_cfr_cash_only_bar (the Code's crew and cash terms; the CFR's other, unamended terms stay in unamended_cfr_cash_prohibition) and is not operative, because a crew member whose only extra pay is non-cash is covered on either reading: in employment under 410(a), or in self-employment under 20 CFR 404.1031(b).

cases.description: 410(a)(22) excludes council-member service for an Indian tribal government except services covered under a section 418a agreement, and 418a(b)(2) defines a tribal council as "the appointed or elected governing body of a federally recognized Indian tribe". POMS RS 01901.700 F covers every service for a tribe that is not federally recognized, council members included, so this case requires recognition; an unrecognized tribe's council member falls to the residual. 418a(b)(1) defines a member as "an individual appointed or elected to serve as a member or the head of the tribal council".
